newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gaddum on Feb 18 - no need for rate cut, dlr okay.
newsitem.headline: Gaddum on Feb 18 - no need for rate cut, dlr okay.

text.p: Johann Wilhelm Gaddum, the deputy president of the German Bundesbank, said he did not see any grounds for a further cut in German interest rates at the moment, adding a cut would not improve the economic climate.

In an interview conducted on February 18, which will be published in the German weekly magazine Boerse Online, Gaddum also said that the Bundesbank and other central banks were fairly happy with the exchange rate of the U.S. dollar.
The dollar was trading at about 1.6850 marks on February 18, slightly higher than its current level of 1.67 marks.
Gaddum on Feb 18 --no need for rate cut, dollar =2

Asked by the magazine, which released the interview ahead of publication this week, how a further fall in the mark from those levels could be prevented, Gaddum said, "the Bundesbank has never set out to prevent prices moving.

"We, along with officials from other central banks, have made clear that at the level which the dollar has now reached it is no longer possible to say that it is undervalued, but rather that it has now achieved a level which we consider appropriate," he said.
"It has now reached a level at which the central banks have signalled interest in the developments. That means that all market participants must realise that they are taking a risk."
On the interest rate outlook, Gaddum said that there would be no justification for a German interest rate cut on the basis of M3 money supply.
"I cannot imagine that we could improve the economic climate further through interest rate cuts," he said.

"Of course it would also not be an obvious decision in view of the exchange rate developments, as an interest rate cut could only further strengthen the dollar as an investment currency," Gaddum added.
